ideas.title: Kingfisher Clarkfork true rotary vise (his main want, best version)
ideas.product_search: Kingfisher Fly Fishing Clarkfork True Rotary Fly Tying Vise Gold
ideas.retailer_hint: Amazon (Kingfisher's own store lists it at $79.95 if Amazon is out of stock)
fits_facts: wants: needs a new rotary fly-tying vise (captured)
constraint: jaws must securely hold size 18 and smaller hooks (captured)
owns: old fly-tying vise, about 20 years old and worn out (captured)
ideas.why: This is the one over-budget pick, at about 7% over, and it is my top choice for his stated need. <cite index="1-9">One review roundup calls it the smoothest true rotary under $100. It has dual ball-bearing housings and hardened tool-steel jaws that hold sizes 26 to 4/0 and grip tiny hooks firmly.</cite> That covers his size 18-and-smaller requirement for trout dry flies. It replaces the worn-out vise, so he isn't getting a duplicate. Check the shipped total at checkout, because the 15% allowance caps it at about $86.

ideas.title: Dr. Slick micro-tip fine scissors for tying small flies
ideas.product_search: Dr. Slick 4 inch Micro Tip Scissors fly tying
fits_facts: interest: dry fly fishing for trout (captured)
ideas.why: Trimming hackle and wing material on size 18 and smaller flies needs a fine tip, and he will have a new vise to hold them. It is one small tool that takes almost no space. A tying guide notes that <cite index="27-13">tying an Adams takes a vise, a bobbin, and fine-tipped scissors for close trimming near the hook.</cite> It pairs well with the vise if you buy both.
